source_title: INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC to be held at Kharge's residence on October 30 - The Hindu
source_excerpt: New Delhi The INDIA bloc will hold its proposed “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s official residence, 10, Rajaji Marg, in New Delhi, at 3.30 p.m. on Friday (October 30, 2026), Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh announced on Wednesday (October 28, 2026). Delhi Police grants Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan with strict conditions, denies mock impeachment request storyline 1 The Congress president’s official residence was decided as the venue after the Opposition bloc’s attempts to organise the event at the Ashok Hotel and Ramlila Maidan allegedly ran into hurdles over permission. Congress alleges hurdles to INDIA bloc’s proposed ‘public impeachment’ of CEC Gyanesh Kumar on October 30 storyline 1 CTI writes to Rahul Gandhi again on INDIA bloc's November 1 rally, seeks meeting CTI writes to Rahul Gandhi again on INDIA bloc's November 1 rally, seeks meeting In a letter to Mr. Gandhi, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said representatives of 20 markets wanted to explain how the proposed rally could disrupt business ahead of Deepavali CTI writes to Rahul Gandhi again on INDIA bloc's November 1 rally, seeks meeting storyline 1 The programme has been planned as a curtain-raiser for the Opposition’s November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan against alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police grants Congress NOC for November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan storyline 1 “The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) has openly violated the spirit and provisions of the Constitution. He has hollowed out the very foundation of our meticulously planned electoral democratic system. In plain words, he has lied to the Supreme Court. Acting on the signals of that venomous duo, he has turned himself into their tool. Their turn will come next,” the Congress’s communications chief said in a post on social media platform X. On Tuesday (October 27, 2026), the Congress had alleged that the authorities were obstructing the event to silence criticism of the Election Commission of India (ECI). Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal claimed that the Ashok Hotel, which had initially granted permission, withdrew it following police intervention. The party subsequently decided to shift the programme to Ramlila Maidan, which it said it had booked from October 25 to November 3. Tell Modi to sack Gyanesh Kumar, protests will stop in 30 seconds: Rahul to traders Tell Modi to sack Gyanesh Kumar, protests will stop in 30 seconds: Rahul to traders The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has urged Mr. Gandhi to postpone the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan until after November 10, warning that it could disrupt business worth ₹10,000 crore during the peak Diwali shopping season Tell Modi to sack Gyanesh Kumar, protests will stop in 30 seconds: Rahul to traders storyline 1 However, Mr. Venugopal alleged that police personnel stopped workers from setting up infrastructure at the venue. “This means it is not the Delhi Police’s decision. It is the decision of PM (Narendra) Modi and (Home Minister) Amit Shah and they are protecting their pet Gyanesh Kumar,” Mr. Venugopal alleged on Tuesday. Responding to the charge Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh had told The Hindu that the Congress had sought permission only for a rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, which had been granted subject to conditions. No separate request for a mock impeachment had been received, Mr. Singh said.
